result:
**Root cause.** `mkHalf` in `variants/bug02/movegen.inc` compared the moved piece type against `WN` (knight, 2) instead of `WP` (pawn, 1), so pawn moves fell through to the increment and knight moves took the reset of the fifty-move clock.

**Files touched**
- `variants/bug02/movegen.inc:908` — `cp WN` → `cp WP` (+2 comments); the whole fix
- `variants/bug02/test_fifty_move.py` — new, 8-case harness-driven regression test
- `variants/bug02/Makefile` — new `test-fifty` target, called from `test:`
- `variants/bug02/BUILD.md` — documents the new test
- `variants/bug02/chess.bin`, `chess.tap` — rebuilt (exactly one byte differs: offset 4354, 0x02→0x01)
- `FIX_NOTES.md`, `STATE.md` at the workspace root

**Gate status**
- Reported symptom no longer reproduces — **pass**. All four "Expected" items hold: hm98 + `a2a3` → 0 and still playing; + `e8e7` → 1 with `Your move`; hm40 + `Na1-b3` → 41; hm99 + one quiet rook move → 100 + `Draw (50-move)`.
- `make test` — **pass** (5 original smoke checks + the new test). It was already green on the buggy build, so it was never a signal for this bug.
- New test — **pass**, 8/8 on the fix; **3 ok / 5 failed** on a tape re-wrapped from the saved pre-fix binary, so it would have caught this.
- `characterisation/characterise.py` — **pass**, 57/57 (was 40 ok / 17 FAIL before the fix, every failure halfmove-shaped). Note: pass `--harness harness`; its built-in default points outside the workspace.
- Code review — **pass**, round 1 of 3: "no defect in the fix". Gate closed at one round.

**Knowingly left open.** The reviewer's N2–N8 are recorded in `FIX_NOTES.md` §5 and not acted on per the termination rule: test coverage gaps (no en-passant/castling/double-push case in the new test — the reviewer verified all of them correct out of band), `gameStateName: draw` not distinguishing draw types by itself, and four pre-existing behaviours this diff does not touch (`SRC` list omits three includes; the search never consults `halfmove`; `resetGameState` does not zero it; a position loaded already at ≥100 only declares the draw on the next move). Also pre-existing and unchanged: `halfmove` has no 255 saturation — unreachable in play, and capping it would deviate from the characterised build. Its N1 (two test cases could pass vacuously) was non-blocking but I took it anyway, pinning the resulting FEN in every case, and re-verified.
